summary: Kodo Yotsuya specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University, studying under Shiro Matsumoto, and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.

Koen Wellens works in Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst works in Indology, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992) and completed an MA at KU Leuven (~1988–1999).

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctorate of Letters at the University of Tokyo in 1928. He served as professor (1940) and president (1976) at Komazawa University, and professor at the University of Tokyo (1959–1962).

Kogi Kudara (1945–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held a professorship at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and an editorial post at Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).
Koichi Furusaka specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Hakuyu Hadano and served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).
Koichi Hiraoka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1984) and held a visiting professorship at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Koichi Hokazono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn, earned a PhD at Kyushu University, and held a professorship at The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991–2000).

Koichi Hoshina (1872–1955) worked in linguistics and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897), he held posts at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education (~1902–1933).

Koichi Shinohara is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He served as a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and later as a senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004).

Koichi Takahashi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (-2004) under Akira Saitō and Yasunori Ejima, and later served there as an assistant (attested 2005) and professor (attested 2026).

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an MA at the University of Tokyo, studying under Akira Hirakawa and Gyoin Hashimoto, and served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1978–2006).
Koin Takada (1924–1998) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Gyoin Hashimoto (~1937–1971), whom he succeeded in 1967, and studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1944).

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara at Kyoto University, became a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969), and worked at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1953–1957) and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University (-1991), where he served as an assistant professor (~1969) and professor (~1978–2005).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sokichi Tsuda at Waseda University. He was a professor at Waseda University (1941–1969) and president of Taisho University (1928–1968; 1972–1975).
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He subsequently served there as an assistant professor (~1970–1978), department chair (~1978–2002), and professor emeritus (~2002).
Koki Kawagishi (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1976, he is attested as holding professorships at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University.
